Week 9 assignment

Arghavan Kassraie

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(GenomicRanges)
  library(epiwraps)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(rGREAT)
  library(rtracklayer)
  library(ComplexHeatmap)
})

Download data

options(timeout = 6000)
download.file(
  "https://ethz-ins.org/content/clustering_assignment.zip",
  "clustering_assignment.zip"
)
unzip("clustering_assignment.zip")

Prepare regions and tracks

tracks <- c(
  "Creb1.bw",
  "Creb3.bw",
  "Creb3L1.bw"
)
peak_files <- c(
  "Creb1.bed",
  "Creb3.bed",
  "Creb3L1.bed"
)
# Import peaks
peaks <- lapply(peak_files, rtracklayer::import.bed)
# Keep high confidence peaks
peaks <- lapply(peaks, function(x) x[x$score > 800])
# Merge regions
regions <- reduce(unlist(GRangesList(peaks)))

Clustering and visualisation

ese <- signal2Matrix(tracks, regions, extend = 2000)
## Reading Creb1.bw
## Reading Creb3.bw
## Reading Creb3L1.bw
set.seed(123)
cl <- clusterSignalMatrices(ese, k = 4)
##   ~66% of the variance explained by clusters
rowData(ese)$cluster <- cl

mycolors <- c("1"="red", "2"="blue", "3"="darkgreen", "4"="black")

plotEnrichedHeatmaps(ese,
                     row_split  = rowData(ese)$cluster,
                     mean_color = mycolors,
                     colors     = c("white", "darkred"),
                     use_raster = FALSE)

GO enrichment on cluster 3

split_regions <- split(
  rowRanges(ese),
  rowData(ese)$cluster
)
res <- great(
  split_regions[["3"]],
  gene_sets  = "GO:BP",
  tss_source = "hg38",
  background = regions,
  cores      = 2
)
## * TSS source: TxDb.
## * check whether TxDb package 'TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene' is installed.
## * gene ID type in the extended TSS is 'Entrez Gene ID'.
## * restrict chromosomes to 'chr1, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5, chr6, chr7, chr8, chr9, chr10,
##     chr11, chr12, chr13, chr14, chr15, chr16, chr17, chr18, chr19, chr20, chr21, chr22, chrX,
##     chrY, chrM'.
## * 18193/35161 protein-coding genes left.
## * update seqinfo to the selected chromosomes.
## * TSS extension mode is 'basalPlusExt'.
## * construct the basal domains by extending 5000bp to upstream and 1000bp to downsteram of TSS.
## * calculate distances to neighbour regions.
## * extend to both sides until reaching the neighbour genes or to the maximal extension.
## * use GO:BP ontology with 15046 gene sets (source: org.Hs.eg.db).
## * check gene ID type in `gene_sets` and in `extended_tss`.
## * use self-defined background regions.
## * remove excluded regions from background.
## * overlap `gr` to background regions (based on midpoint).
## * in total 450 `gr`.
## * overlap extended TSS to background regions.
## * check which genes are in the gene sets.
## * only take gene sets with size >= 5.
## * in total 2479 gene sets.
## * overlap `gr` to every extended TSS.
## * perform binomial test for each biological term.
bp <- getEnrichmentTables(res)
ggplot(
  head(bp, 15),
  aes(
    fold_enrichment,
    reorder(description, p_adjust),
    size  = observed_region_hits,
    color = -log10(p_adjust)
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "GO Enrichment Analysis – Cluster 3",
    x = "Fold enrichment",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()

Cluster 1 is primarily driven by Creb1-specific binding, whereas Cluster 3 shows binding mainly exclusive to Creb3. In contrast, Cluster 2 highlights shared binding sites strongly occupied by all three factors, and Cluster 4 represents regions co bounded by Creb1 and Creb3L1 with minimal Creb3 involvement. GO enrichment analysis of cluster 3 reveals over representation of terms related to cellular response to stimulus, cell communication, and cell surface receptor signaling, consistent with Creb3’s role as a stress responsive transcription factor. Together, these results show that while CREB-family members share many binding sites, Creb3 and Creb3L1 each occupy distinct binding profiles reflecting their specific biological roles.
